c1-16-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Heated Debate
c1-16-01.scenario: Károly asks how the debate between the two parties went.
c1-16-01.prompt: Tell Károly that it was heated, but that the parties still listened to each other.
cues: Say what the parties still did
c1-16-01.target: A vita heves volt, mindazonáltal a felek meghallgatták egymást.
c1-16-01.english: The debate was heated; nevertheless the parties listened to each other.
c1-16-01.canDo: I can grant a point in a public debate with *mindazonáltal* or *annak ellenére, hogy*.

c1-16-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Question for the Audience
c1-16-02.scenario: At a meeting about the press, Károly asks you to say something that makes the audience think.
c1-16-02.prompt: Ask a rhetorical question about a debate and a free press.
cues: Open with a word that marks a rhetorical question
Name the two things in the question
c1-16-02.target: Vajon elképzelhető-e valódi vita szabad sajtó nélkül?
c1-16-02.english: Is a real debate conceivable without a free press?
c1-16-02.canDo: I can ask a rhetorical question in a political text (*vajon …?, nemde éppen …?*).

c1-16-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Report Says
c1-16-03.scenario: Károly asks what the audit report says about a question that is still unclear and about the errors it found.
c1-16-03.prompt: Tell Károly what is to be done.
cues: Say what is still to be clarified
c1-16-03.target: A kérdés még tisztázandó, a hibák pedig kivizsgálásra szorulnak.
c1-16-03.english: The question is still to be clarified, and the errors need investigation.
c1-16-03.canDo: I can say that something is still to be done with *-andó/-endő* (*tisztázandó*).

c1-16-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Does the News Come From
c1-16-04.scenario: Károly asks where a news report gets its information.
c1-16-04.prompt: Name the source and say what the report claims.
cues: Name the source of the information
c1-16-04.target: Információink szerint a döntést már előbb meghozták.
c1-16-04.english: According to our information, the decision had been made earlier.
c1-16-04.canDo: I can name the source of a news claim (*információink szerint, állítólag*).

c1-16-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Fear and Freedom
c1-16-05.scenario: You have read the text about Bibó István. Károly asks what it says about fear.
c1-16-05.prompt: Tell Károly what the text says about fear and freedom.
cues: Say what is hard in a climate of fear
Say who says it, according to the text
c1-16-05.target: A szöveg szerint a félelem légkörében nehéz szabadnak lenni.
c1-16-05.english: According to the text, it is hard to be free in a climate of fear.
c1-16-05.canDo: I can add a background to a sentence with a *-va/-ve* participle (*a félelmeket elemezve*).

c1-16-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Summing Up the Public Sphere
c1-16-consolidation.scenario: Károly asks you to sum up a report you have read about a bill.
c1-16-consolidation.prompt: Grant a point about the bill and say what is to happen to the errors.
cues: Grant that the bill is not flawless
c1-16-consolidation.target: A javaslat nem hibátlan, mindazonáltal fontos előrelépés.
c1-16-consolidation.english: The proposal is not flawless; nevertheless it is an important step forward.
c1-16-consolidation.canDo: I can grant a point and ask a rhetorical question about public life.
